extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners advising on USPTO practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for detecting, framing, and avoiding statutory and nonstatutory double patenting rejections, including when to use form paragraphs, when terminal disclaimers apply, and how double patenting interacts with prior art rejections and 35 U.S.C. 121 restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the rule against double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental reason for the rule is to prevent unjustified timewise extension of the right to exclude granted by a patent; burden is on appellant to establish that the invention claimed is 'independent and distinct' from the invention of the appealed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is not limited to identical claims (e.g., ABCX vs ABCY are technically different inventions) but focuses on preventing extension of exclusionary rights; see In re Schneller (397 F.2d 350).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory double patenting based on In re Schneller
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections based on the Schneller fact pattern are limited and should be rare; Schneller-type nonstatutory double patenting rejections require special handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an examiner determines such a rejection is appropriate they must first consult their SPE, and if SPE agrees, obtain TC Director approval before issuing a nonstatutory double patenting rejection based on Schneller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.38 — Nonstatutory DP (with an issued patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when claim [1] is rejected over claim [2] of U.S. Patent No. [3] because allowance would improperly extend the 'right to exclude' already granted in the patent; subject matter must be fully disclosed in and covered by at least one claim of the issued patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.33 must precede it and be used only once per Office action. Use only where TC Director approval for Schneller-based rejections has been obtained (when applicable). Fill bracket 3 with the patent number and bracket 4 with a description of the covered subject matter. Additional examiner notes list when to add related statutory rejections for pre-AIA/AIA cases (e.g., 102(f)/(g), 102(e)/103(a), or 102(a)(2)/103).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.39 — Provisional nonstatutory DP (with another application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use to provisionally reject claim [1] over claim [2] of a copending Application No. [3] because the claims are patentably indistinct and would be covered by a patent granted on the copending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.33 must precede it and be used only once. Use only where TC Director approval for Schneller-based rejections has been obtained (when applicable). Fill bracket 3 with the copending application number and bracket 4 with the overlapping subject matter description. Examiner notes instruct additional rejections or use of other form paragraphs for pre-AIA/AIA situations, and require making a provisional DP rejection in the copending application as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design/plant vs utility double patenting principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting principles applied in utility-utility situations generally apply to utility-plant and utility-design situations; double patenting rejections may be made in appropriate circumstances across these categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law shows both affirmances and reversals depending on whether inventions are the same or obvious variations. In design-utility cases courts have sometimes required a two-way obviousness determination; examine facts of each case individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between double patenting and prior art (35 U.S.C. 102/103) rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting rejections must rely on comparison with the claims in an issued or to-be-issued patent, whereas 102(e)/103(a) rejections rely on what the reference patent discloses (claimed or unclaimed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A terminal disclaimer cannot be used to obviate a 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) rejection. For commonly owned references, consider 35 U.S.C. 103(c) disqualification; examiners should be aware of differences in available bases (claims vs disclosure) when framing rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: When examiner should also make 35 U.S.C. 102/103 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner should make both a 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) rejection (if appropriate) and a double patenting rejection when the facts support both rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner omits a separately applicable rejection and includes it in the next action, that next Office action cannot be made final. For AIA/pre-AIA distinctions see specific MPEP cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification of commonly assigned/owned patents as prior art (35 U.S.C. 103(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain filing dates and circumstances a commonly assigned/owned patent or application may be disqualified as 102(e) prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(1) or via evidence of a joint research agreement under 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2)/(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As alternatives to invoking 103(c), applicants may file applications on the same day, merge copending applications, or submit affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.132/1.131 (subject to limitations). See MPEP §§ 716.10, 715, 718 for affidavit/declaration practice and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer cannot obviate statutory double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer is not effective to overcome a statutory type double patenting rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory double patenting must be overcome by claim amendments to remove coextensiveness, canceling conflicting claims, or canceling all but one of the conflicting pending applications' claims. 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits are inappropriate for statutory double patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer as remedy for nonstatutory double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonstatutory double patenting rejection can generally be obviated by filing a terminal disclaimer in the application or proceeding in which the rejection is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a terminal disclaimer encourages disclosure and earlier expiration of patents; case law supports its use (e.g., In re Vogel, In re Knohl, In re Griswold). The terminal disclaimer must meet regulatory requirements (37 CFR 1.321) and may include common ownership/unenforceability provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits for double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit is inappropriate to overcome a double patenting rejection when the claims of the application and patent are 'directed to substantially the same invention' or where there is lack of 'patentable distinctness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law (In re Dunn; Knell v. Muller; In re Ward; In re Teague; In re Hidy) supports that 1.131 cannot substitute for a terminal disclaimer or eliminate double patenting where claims are essentially the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition on using patent from restriction as reference
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibits using a patent issuing on an application that was subject to an Office restriction requirement as a reference against any divisional application filed as a result of that restriction, provided the divisional was filed before the patent issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibition applies only where the Office made a requirement for restriction; does not apply to voluntarily filed divisionals. The prohibition covers typical restriction categories (combination/subcombination, process/apparatus/product combinations, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition does not apply (A–G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific exceptions include: (A) applicant voluntarily filed multiple applications without a restriction requirement; (B) claims not consonant with restriction requirement due to material changes; (C) restriction was written subject to nonallowance of generic/linking claims and such claims later allowed (requiring withdrawal); (D) restriction made only in an international application by ISR/IPEA; (E) restriction withdrawn by examiner before patent issues; (F) claims of second app. drawn to the 'same invention' as the first; (G) certain product/process restriction-withdrawal situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In each instance examine whether the divisional claims were formally entered and restricted/removed in the earlier application and whether the examiner's restriction line was maintained (consonance). Case law cited: Geneva Pharms., Symbol, Gerber, Studiengesellschaft Kohle, Bristol-Myers Squibb, Ziegler.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding statutory double patenting (practical measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory double patenting can be avoided by amending conflicting claims so they are not coextensive, canceling conflicting claims in pending applications, or canceling claims in all but one pending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimers are ineffective against statutory double patenting; 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits are inappropriate. Cited cases include In re Dunn, Knell v. Muller, In re Ward, In re Teague, In re Hidy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding nonstatutory double patenting (practical measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonstatutory double patenting rejection can be avoided by filing a terminal disclaimer in the application or proceeding where the rejection is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimers encourage disclosure and earlier availability to the public; supporting case law includes In re Jentoft, In re Eckel, In re Braithwaite. Terminal disclaimers must comply with 37 CFR 1.321 and MPEP §1490 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and form of a terminal disclaimer (37 CFR 1.321)
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer is a statement filed by an owner to disclaim or dedicate a portion of the entire term of all claims of a patent; requirements are set out in 37 CFR 1.321 and sample forms/guidance in MPEP §1490.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A terminal disclaimer must operate with respect to all claims in the patent (cannot disclaim only specified claims). For commonly owned conflicting claims, the disclaimer must include a provision that the patent is enforceable only while commonly owned (37 CFR 1.321(c)). 37 CFR 1.321(d) sets requirements where the invention resulted from a joint research agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimers for multiple conflicting references
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple conflicting patents and/or pending applications are applied in an application, before issuance it is necessary to disclaim the terminal part of any patent granted that would extend beyond the application date of each conflicting patent/application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single terminal disclaimer based on common ownership or based on a joint research agreement may be filed to cover all commonly owned conflicts to avoid multiple fees, but each conflicting commonly owned reference must be included in the disclaimer to avoid dual-ownership problems if common ownership later ceases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirements for continuing applications filed on/after June 8, 1995
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuing utility or plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 (20-year term rules of 35 U.S.C. 154(a)(2)), a terminal disclaimer is required to overcome nonstatutory double patenting rejections because patents may have differing term expirations and patent term extension considerations under 35 U.S.C. 154(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimers must include common-ownership enforceability provisions (37 CFR 1.321(c)(3)) and follow 1.321(d) rules for joint research agreements to avoid harassment by multiple parties with patents claiming patentably indistinct inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner practice when a disqualified prior-art reference becomes basis for DP rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Until applicant establishes the existence of a joint research agreement or other disqualifying evidence, the examiner cannot apply a double patenting rejection based on the possible existence of such an agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant later disqualifies a relied-upon reference under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) in reply to a 102/103 rejection and a subsequent double patenting rejection based on the disqualified reference is applied, the next Office action may be made final even without claim amendment, provided no new ground of rejection is introduced that was not necessitated by amendment or an IDS filed within the 1.97(c) period.
